wording: A numerical solver can diverge from a true solution: for forward Euler a perturbation is multiplied by (1 + a h) each step, so it grows when |1 + a h| > 1; on the simple harmonic oscillator the growth factor |1 +/- i h w0| exceeds 1 for every h > 0, so the computed solution always grows. Stability depends on both the solver and the ODE.
verification_phrases: P17|the solution computed by forward Euler always grows || P17|the property of stability depends upon both the solver and the ODE itself

wording: In a branching-growth toy, driver mutations were over-represented among high-frequency (CCF >= 0.5) mutations relative to low-frequency ones (0.21 vs 0.12 with driver effect 0.5; 0.19 vs 0.10 with 1.0), so the pre-registered 2-fold enrichment was not supported. In the neutral control none of 41 high-CCF mutations was a driver (0.046 among low-CCF); the 'no difference' test was not supported only because a zero share gives a zero binomial SE, a flaw in the test, not evidence of depletion.
confidence: Low-moderate (40 tumours each; few high-CCF mutations)
counterevidence_limits: Non-spatial toy; whole-population CCF; binomial SE ignores clone structure and is degenerate at zero.
operationalization: Divergence = selection shaping which branches become clonal
